ul.li: DMIBAR, PXPEPBAR, EDRAMBAR, GTXVTBAR, DFDBAR registers are removed.

Memory Map and Bar Initialization:
BIOS need to configure below bars in NCU (accessible on Device 0 function 0). Register interface remains same as previous programs. Refer to section System Memory Map for overall memory map.
VTDBAR(MCHBAR+0x5410) size:512KB
NVL expose the 2 IOMMUs on compute i.e. graphics and non-gfx each of 64KB size.
Separate 64KB IOMMU bar for IOC0 hosted VTd engine.
Legacy DMIBAR (BAR exists but no registers behind its BIOS must leave this disabled)
SAFBAR(B0D0F0+0x68) size:32MB (only need pre-BIOS done NOT needed after BIOS done)
REGBAR 128MB -> Used for SB transactions.
PMBAR 4x in size (32kB->128kB) - Dev10 bar handled within PCI enumeration and for temporary PCI enumeration for telemetry 128KB size needed.

NoHom range introduction:
BIOS must program NoHOM.BASE and NoHOM.LIMIT above 4GB range in offset 0x90 and 0x98 in Hostbridge
BIOS must ensure MCHBAR, REGBAR and SAFBAR are mapped within the NoHOM range - Mcheck checks if this range includes (MCHBAR, SAFBAR, REGBAR)
BIOS must calculate the size of the range by reading registers to determine the end of C-Die BAR (SNCU_NCDECS_CR_CDIEBAREND_0_0_0_MCHBAR)
MCHBAR, REGBAR, SAFBAR must not overlap and all must be after CdieBARend
BIOS must program TOLUD, TOM, TOUUD based on correct amount of memory
BIOS should not program PCIEXBAR, NOHOME between 0-TOLUD, or 4G-TOM

CBO MC Bank clearing on NEM exit -
No need for BIOS to clear MCA banks after NEM exit. CCF will block logging and triggering of WbtoMMIO MCA during NEM.

PAM range registers are removed:
BIOS must remove the PAM register programming to configure it to DRAM vs MMIO
BIOS must remove the PAM lock programming
PAM registers are set to harcoded registers to '11'(HOM) and the lock bits are set to '1'. No other value of PAM will be supported.

Dev0 CFG Initialization:
All the Device0 Cfg programing ( GSM, DSM, TOLUD, TOUUD, TOM) will be done in NCU. From SW perspective, there is no impact or change as these still remains in BDF- 0/0/0 with same offset.

IMR programming:
When BIOS programs the IMR registers using MCHBAR + MCAST_IMR, sNCU claims the cycle and does HW-multicast to all protocol bridges and relevant IPs including IOC.

Device Enable/Disable:
There is new CAPID/DEVEN/BDF_ALLOC register mapping added starting LNL/PTL in C-die to map IP's 1:1 in CAPID, DEVEN and BDF_ALLOC. BIOS need to use new CAPID/DEVEN register for all IP enable/disable configuration and reading IP fuse status through CAPID i.e. IGD, NPU, IAX, IPU, PMT/Telemetry, Camarillo, VMD IP's. BDF_ALLOC not required to be programmed by BIOS , since device BDF's on MH are fixed and doesn't support function remapping. However, for PCIe root ports, BIOS need to use BDF_ALLOC for function remapping when F0 is disabled.

sNCU has 4 different 4 byte scratchpads accessible to all threads in the system exposed through MCHBAR:
scratchpad_0_0_0_mchbar_ncu0
scratchpad_0_0_0_mchbar_ncu1
scratchpad_0_0_0_mchbar_ncu2
scratchpad_0_0_0_mchbar_ncu3
PLAT_CONFIG - This register is not used and can be removed at designs convenience.

Mcheck Summary:
None of the following ranges can overlap or overlap with memory:
PCIEXBAR
NoHOMEBASE - CDIEBAREND
MCHBAR - MCHBAR+256KB-1
VTDBAR - VTDBAR+512KB-1
SAFBAR - SAFBAR+32MB-1
MCHBAR and SAFBAR must overlap (CIDEBAREND+1 - NoHOMELIMIT) but not each other.

MCHBAR regs duplicated into Cdiebar
6800h - 6BFFh (1KB) Registers in this range of MCHBAR programmed by BIOS will now need to be programed in MCHBAR AND in each CDIEBAR (unless instructed otherwise).
